title: Is there an option to generate 3d models locally?
author: NecessaryBSHappens
selftext: I am looking for a solution to run a local AI model for image and low-poly 3d generation. Does not need to be great, just something I can use for free on my own and potentially without connection. But everything I found so far is purely online and paid

comments.author: Standard_Text480
comments.body:
yes, install blender and tell it that. but don’t leave it too open to generate, might want to create a plan first on what you’re building that it can follow.

for example, my plan says before building the ship hull, research 3 perspectives of the ship.

replies.author: zreakz
replies.body: How do you tell blender to generate something?

replies.author: PedroArthurPA
replies.body: You don't tell blender, you connect it with a MCP and tells your AI what you want

comments.author: Kingnorik
comments.body: Trellis 2.0. You need a nvidia card with like 8gb vram at the very least. And it'll look like last years commercial 3d generators.

replies.author: futuneral
replies.body: It can do ok models, but texturing is kind of weak. On the flip side - it's free and local, you got more than you paid for!

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: Local 3D is cool, but unless it's for some static, it's pretty useless and will give you a terribly unoptimized mesh with tons of issues that usually need to be cleaned up in post.

comments.author: pspahn
comments.body:
I experimented with this a little bit yesterday. Results are okay.

I wanted some procedural low poly tree models of many different species. I started with some image gens of low poly tree models in nano banana and then gave claude+blender those images to build the models procedurally. 

Then turned that into a proper module than I can just run any time to generate new models. 

Probably not quite what you're after, but it's been useful and the models are fine for where I'm currently at.
